answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks using bonded staking at the network wharf, requiring participants to lock slashable collateral before submitting tasks. Evaluated through an economic prism, identity is anchored to scarce liquid capital rather than virtual runtimes, forcing attackers to incur a linear financial lockup per forged node. While this resists a severe gale of synthetic identities, it creates capital barriers that marginalize low-balance autonomous agents.
